correctness.rationale: The necessity proof is direct: the bounded adjoint maps normalized coherent kernels to a finite sum; along generic complex rays the Gram matrix is asymptotically block-diagonal by unitary part. Within a block, coherent states at distinct translation centers have a strictly positive fixed Gram minimum under common Weyl displacement; between blocks Gaussian overlap tends to zero uniformly as the ray parameter escapes. Hence each Gaussian-compensated entire coefficient is bounded on every such ray; Liouville and density of generic rays force it to be constant. The converse uses Gaussian isometry. Exact normalized-ball coherent-state squared-norm averaging eliminates off-diagonal terms by Gaussian dominated convergence for different unitary parts and Riemann–Lebesgue for equal unitary parts with different shifts. Weak escape of coherent kernels kills all compact operators; quadratic cyclic chirps attain the sharp coefficient 1 for every N and d. A deterministic checker passed 9448 supplementary assertions, not substituted for these infinite-dimensional proofs.

Tien–Khoi (2018) treats one weighted composition in several variables. Two later November 2026 papers classify finite weighted sums only in one variable, and are compared but not used to establish this theorem. Complete published mathematical research records inspected about weighted translations, Toeplitz representation of finite centered dilations, and Weyl displacements concern different objects and domains; one previously recorded finding on the same Bayart paper concerns small-time norm of a diagonal contracting semigroup, not weighted sums. No checked statement implies the new multivariable finite-family claim. Priority risk from older or abstract-equivalent literature remains.
